On Wed, Jun 20, 2012 at 1:20 PM, dtenenba <dand...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hello,
> I changed some of the Rhipe examples from the github wiki to do what I want
> to do, and it works, but it looks like the mapper only runs once, instead of
> once per piece of input data which is what I would like.
> It's also possible that the way I have put my code together is not well
> thought-out.
>
> What I did was change the word count generator example to generate some
> strings of input data to process.
> Then I created another mapreduce job, based on the word count example (with
> no reduce function, because I don't need one) which takes a piece of that
> input data and does some processing to it and then writes out some output.
> It works but it seems, judging from the output, that the mapper only ran
> once.
>
> I realize that maybe I should change this to a single mapreduce job, where
> the mapper runs just once and creates all the input data, and the reducer
> processes it. I have tried that and run into problems. So I thought it would
> be best to post about what actually works and ask how I can get it to work
> the proper number of times, and then maybe incrementally get to a better way
> of doing it.
>
> So first, off, some dependencies are required in order to do this, if you
> want to try it yourself:
> You must be running R-2.15.
> Do the following:
> source("http://bioconductor.org/biocLite.R")
> useDevel()
> biocLite(c("snpStats", "VariantAnnotation",
> "TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene"))
>
> Outside of R, do this (because this package is not part of Bioconductor):
> svn co --username readonly --password
> readonly https://hedgehog.fhcrc.org/bioconductor/trunk/madman/Rpacks/BiocCloud/
> R CMD INSTALL BiocCloud
> (if the above step complains about missing dependencies, install them)
>
> Now, here is what actually works:
>
> Step 1, generate input data:
>
> library(Rhipe)
> rhinit()
>
> makeDataSet <- function(N, dest, local=TRUE)
> {
>     map <- as.expression(bquote({
>         N <- .(N)
>         urls <- getBucketUrls()
>         txdb <- TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene
>         cds <- cds(txdb)
>         cds <- reduce(keepSeqlevels(cds, paste("chr", 1:22, sep="")))
>         values(cds)[["Url"]] <- urls[as.character(seqnames(cds))]
>         map <- setNames(sub("chr", "", seqlevels(cds)), seqlevels(cds))
>         cds <- renameSeqlevels(cds, map)
>         ## Return a regular R list
>         tasks <- Map(function(...) list(...),
>             seqnames=as.character(seqnames(cds)), start=start(cds),
>             end=end(cds), url=values(cds)$Url,
> MoreArgs=list(genome=unique(genome(cds))))
>
>         if (N > length(tasks)) N <- length(tasks)
>
>
>         for (i in 1:N)
>         {
>             row = tasks[[i]]
>             line <- sprintf("%s %s %s %s %s", row$seqnames, row$start,
> row$end,
>                 row$url, row$genome)
>             rhcollect(NULL, line)
>         }
>
>     }, list()))
>     mapred <- list()
>     if (local) mapred$mapred.job.tracker <- 'local'
>     mapred$mapred.field.separator=" "
>     mapred$mapred.textoutputformat.usekey=FALSE
>     mapred$mapred.map.tasks=1
>     z <- rhmr(map=map, N=N,ofolder=dest,inout=c("lapp","text"),
>          mapred=mapred,
>          setup=list(map=expression({
>              suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(BiocCloud))
>              suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(VariantAnnotation))
>
>  suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene))
>              suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(snpStats))
>          })))
>     rhex(z)
>
> }
>
> N <- 10
> filename <- sprintf("/tmp/%s",paste(sample(letters,6),collapse=""))
> makeDataSet(N,filename)
> message(sprintf("Input created in %s",filename))
>
> That works and creates a file in the 'filename' directory that looks like
> this:
> 1 12190 12227
> http://s3.amazonaws.com/1000genomes/release/20101123/interim_phase1_release/ALL.chr1.phase1.projectConsensus.genotypes.vcf.gz
> hg19
> 1 12595 12721
> http://s3.amazonaws.com/1000genomes/release/20101123/interim_phase1_release/ALL.chr1.phase1.projectConsensus.genotypes.vcf.gz
> hg19
> 1 13403 13639
> http://s3.amazonaws.com/1000genomes/release/20101123/interim_phase1_release/ALL.chr1.phase1.projectConsensus.genotypes.vcf.gz
> hg19
> 1 69091 70008
> http://s3.amazonaws.com/1000genomes/release/20101123/interim_phase1_release/ALL.chr1.phase1.projectConsensus.genotypes.vcf.gz
> hg19
> 1 324343 324345
> http://s3.amazonaws.com/1000genomes/release/20101123/interim_phase1_release/ALL.chr1.phase1.projectConsensus.genotypes.vcf.gz
> hg19
> 1 324439 325605
> http://s3.amazonaws.com/1000genomes/release/20101123/interim_phase1_release/ALL.chr1.phase1.projectConsensus.genotypes.vcf.gz
> hg19
> 1 327746 328213
> http://s3.amazonaws.com/1000genomes/release/20101123/interim_phase1_release/ALL.chr1.phase1.projectConsensus.genotypes.vcf.gz
> hg19
> 1 367659 368597
> http://s3.amazonaws.com/1000genomes/release/20101123/interim_phase1_release/ALL.chr1.phase1.projectConsensus.genotypes.vcf.gz
> hg19
> 1 861322 861393
> http://s3.amazonaws.com/1000genomes/release/20101123/interim_phase1_release/ALL.chr1.phase1.projectConsensus.genotypes.vcf.gz
> hg19
> 1 865535 865716
> http://s3.amazonaws.com/1000genomes/release/20101123/interim_phase1_release/ALL.chr1.phase1.projectConsensus.genotypes.vcf.gz
> hg19
>
>
> ## Step 2, process the input data
>
>
> map <- expression({
>     geno <- "GT"
>     line <- unlist(strsplit(unlist(map.values)," "))
>     seqnames <- line[1]
>     start <- as.numeric(line[2])
>     end <- as.numeric(line[3])
>     url <- line[4]
>     genome <- line[5]
>
>     gr <- GRanges(seqnames=seqnames,
>         ranges=IRanges(start=start, end=end))
>     param <- ScanVcfParam(fixed=c("REF", "ALT"), info=NA, geno=geno,
>                           which=gr)
>
>     tab <- open(TabixFile(url))
>     on.exit(close(tab))
>
>     vcf <- readVcf(tab, unique(genome), param=param)
>     result <- NULL
>     if (nrow(vcf)) {
>         snpm <- MatrixToSnpMatrix(geno(vcf)[[geno]],
>                                   values(fixed(vcf))$REF,
>                                   values(fixed(vcf))$ALT)
>         result <- col.summary(snpm$genotypes)$z.HWE
>     } else result <- numeric()
>     keyStr = sprintf("%s %d %d %s %s",
>         seqnames, start, end, url, genome)
>     valueStr <- character()
>     if (length(result)) {
>         valueStr <- paste(result, collapse=" ")
>     } else {
>         valueStr <- "numeric()"
>     }
>     rhcollect(keyStr, valueStr)
> })
>
> outfile <- sprintf("%s-out",filename)
>
>
> z <- rhmr(map=map, reduce=NA, inout=c("text","sequence")
>           ,ifolder=filename
>           ,ofolder=outfile,
>           mapred=list(mapred.map.tasks=100),
>           setup=list(map=expression({
>                suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(VariantAnnotation))
>                suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(snpStats))
>            })))
>
>
> rhex(z,async=FALSE)
>
> results <- rhread(outfile)
>
> So the idea is that the first mapreduce step writes out some input data, and
> then the second mapreduce step has a mapper that each time it runs, looks
> at
> a different line of the input data, and writes out a key-value pair where
> the key is the original line of input data, and the value is some
> calculation performed
> with that input data.
>
> These are the results:
>> results
> [[1]]
> [[1]][[1]]
> [1] "1 12190 12227
> http://s3.amazonaws.com/1000genomes/release/20101123/interim_phase1_release/ALL.chr1.phase1.projectConsensus.genotypes.vcf.gz
> hg19"
>
> [[1]][[2]]
> [1] "28.2006931118756 16.6548562936464 6.55952056101008"
>
> I was hoping there would be 10 results instead of 1 as there were 10 lines
> of input data. I tried to force the mapper to run more than once by setting
> mapred.map.tasks but that didn't seem to work.
>
> As I said, I realize this is an awkward way of doing things and I am open to
> suggestions on how to do it better. But since it "almost" works, I would
> welcome some advice for getting it to actually work, and would then be
>  better able to refine the entire process.
>
> Thanks,
> Dan
>

On Wednesday, June 20, 2012 1:20:04 PM UTC-7, dtenenba wrote:
Hello,
I changed some of the Rhipe examples from the github wiki to do what I want to do, and it works, but it looks like the mapper only runs once, instead of once per piece of input data which is what I would like.
It's also possible that the way I have put my code together is not well thought-out. 

What I did was change the word count generator example to generate some strings of input data to process. 
Then I created another mapreduce job, based on the word count example (with no reduce function, because I don't need one) which takes a piece of that input data and does some processing to it and then writes out some output.
It works but it seems, judging from the output, that the mapper only ran once. 

I realize that maybe I should change this to a single mapreduce job, where the mapper runs just once and creates all the input data, and the reducer processes it. I have tried that and run into problems. So I thought it would be best to post about what actually works and ask how I can get it to work the proper number of times, and then maybe incrementally get to a better way of doing it.

So first, off, some dependencies are required in order to do this, if you want to try it yourself:
You must be running R-2.15.
Do the following:
source("http://bioconductor.org/biocLite.R")
useDevel()
biocLite(c("snpStats", "VariantAnnotation", "TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene"))

Outside of R, do this (because this package is not part of Bioconductor):
svn co --username readonly --password readonly https://hedgehog.fhcrc.org/bioconductor/trunk/madman/Rpacks/BiocCloud/
R CMD INSTALL BiocCloud
(if the above step complains about missing dependencies, install them)

Now, here is what actually works:

Step 1, generate input data:

library(Rhipe)
rhinit()

makeDataSet <- function(N, dest, local=TRUE)
{
    map <- as.expression(bquote({
        N <- .(N)
        urls <- getBucketUrls()

I haven't got around to it, but i will, this week. sorry for the delay.
as for this, if you have N files, you;llhave >=N splits.
But as you pointed out you don't want 200K files. Correct.

But if you have a file with 200K lines, it's most likely going to be
<= 1 block size (e.g. 128MB).
Each block is a map. So if you have 1 block, you'll have 1 map.

Now, depending on how long the computation is you can have M mappers
among which you schedule N lines
e.g. like N/M lines of text. Which means you'd have to have not 200K
files, but maybe 1000 files.
(which in my opinion is too large).

Then use rhmr(map,N=N (here N=200K),
mapred=list(mapred.map.tasks=1000)) and in the map compute the line
corresponding to i.

(setting mapped.map.tasks=N, is not such a good idea if the time taken
to compute for N is smaller than the time taken
to start the map task, this is true for many task distributers).

(at least) read from Hbase. then you're do as above
and for key=i (i-1...N), read the i'th row from an Hbase table.

With respect to the serialization bit GRanges is an S4 class. Rhipe
cannot handle S4 classes.

1) The Bioconductor packages essentially have random read access to the URLs, so they can just download the parts we are interested in, without needing to download everything.
2) My cluster is in Amazon EC2 in the same data center where the 1000genomes data is hosted, so network latency should be low. ("Moving the compute to the data").

Here's what I would suggest, just download the first file:
http://s3.amazonaws.com/1000genomes/release/20101123/interim_phase1_release/ALL.chr1.phase1.projectConsensus.genotypes.vcf.gz
Then just use the first input file (hweoutput_1.txt) which only refers to that url. Make as many copies of it as you need in order to have the appropriate number of input rows. Move the .gz file to a web server that is accessible from the cluster and edit the URL accordingly. The file is 1389 MB.

Thank you!
Dan

Hi,

Tried a demo run with and changed the last few lines to [2]. Notice I
serialize this but I found out they are all plain numeric
vectors, so really no need to serialize.(you mentioned something about
GRanges, i'm working on incorporating other R data types
e.g. S4 classes, expressions, environments, closures etc).

Anyways, for the file rhipe/hweoutput_1.txt (1000 lines), I ran with
100 splits, so 10 in sequence on a cluster with ~230 parallel jobs.
It took about a minute and 30 secs.

Notice these ALL.chr1.phase1.projectConsensus.genotypes.vcf.gz files
are GB sizes - and you mentioned error 139 (which is a segfault)
- does your ec2 cluster have enough memory per node? How many can be
run in parallel?

My nodes typically have 24-48 GB.

Anyways, this looks fun, i'll test it out again using your code( i
modified the code to use shared files and i downloaded [1] and the tbi
file to the cluster I work on)

I can't do exactly your code since i dont have NLIneInputFormat available ...

Btw, when dont use shared files and instead directly access S3, I get
a tabix error and then 139 segfault - i'm not sure why - cluster is
down right now.
(Instead, try download the file using download.file and it's
associated tbi file, call TabixFile on this local file and in the
on.exit delete the file)
Can't check till tomorrow.

Regards
Saptarshi


[1]/ALL.chr1.phase1.projectConsensus.genotypes.vcf.gz

[2]
rhcounter("FileDownloaded","tabixfile",1)

result <- NULL
if (nrow(vcf)) {
snpm <- MatrixToSnpMatrix(geno(vcf)[[geno]],
values(fixed(vcf))$REF,
values(fixed(vcf))$ALT)
result <- serialize(col.summary(snpm$genotypes)$z.HWE,NULL)

} else result <- numeric()
keyStr = sprintf("%s %d %d %s %s",
seqnames, start, end, url, genome)
return(list(class(result), result))

Another thing is to carefully choose the N, the number of tasks. There
192704 tasks,
if one chooses 10K splits, then each has 19 and one has an extra of 2K.
It appears the best split is 4700, since each gets 41 and one gets another 4.

This is a integer optimization problem.

It is also different from a queuing system where nodes pull of from a
queue - in Hadoop
it is preassigned.

Regards
Saptarshi

parts: On Thursday, June 21, 2012 1:50:04 AM UTC+5:30, dtenenba wrote:

Hello,
I changed some of the Rhipe examples from the github wiki to do what I want to do, and it works, but it looks like the mapper only runs once, instead of once per piece of input data which is what I would like.
It's also possible that the way I have put my code together is not well thought-out. 

What I did was change the word count generator example to generate some strings of input data to process. 
Then I created another mapreduce job, based on the word count example (with no reduce function, because I don't need one) which takes a piece of that input data and does some processing to it and then writes out some output.
It works but it seems, judging from the output, that the mapper only ran once. 

I realize that maybe I should change this to a single mapreduce job, where the mapper runs just once and creates all the input data, and the reducer processes it. I have tried that and run into problems. So I thought it would be best to post about what actually works and ask how I can get it to work the proper number of times, and then maybe incrementally get to a better way of doing it.

So first, off, some dependencies are required in order to do this, if you want to try it yourself:
You must be running R-2.15.
Do the following:

source("http://bioconductor.org/biocLite.R")
useDevel()

biocLite(c("snpStats", "VariantAnnotation", "TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene"))

Outside of R, do this (because this package is not part of Bioconductor):
svn co --username readonly --password readonly https://hedgehog.fhcrc.org/bioconductor/trunk/madman/Rpacks/BiocCloud/
R CMD INSTALL BiocCloud
(if the above step complains about missing dependencies, install them)

Now, here is what actually works:

Step 1, generate input data:

library(Rhipe)
rhinit()

makeDataSet <- function(N, dest, local=TRUE)
{
    map <- as.expression(bquote({
        N <- .(N)
        urls <- getBucketUrls()
        txdb <- TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene
        cds <- cds(txdb)
        cds <- reduce(keepSeqlevels(cds, paste("chr", 1:22, sep="")))
        values(cds)[["Url"]] <- urls[as.character(seqnames(cds))]
        map <- setNames(sub("chr", "", seqlevels(cds)), seqlevels(cds))
        cds <- renameSeqlevels(cds, map)
        ## Return a regular R list
        tasks <- Map(function(...) list(...), 
            seqnames=as.character(seqnames(cds)), start=start(cds), 
            end=end(cds), url=values(cds)$Url, MoreArgs=list(genome=unique(genome(cds))))

        if (N > length(tasks)) N <- length(tasks)


        for (i in 1:N)
        {
            row = tasks[[i]]
            line <- sprintf("%s %s %s %s %s", row$seqnames, row$start, row$end,
                row$url, row$genome)
            rhcollect(NULL, line)
        }
        
    }, list()))
    mapred <- list()
    if (local) mapred$mapred.job.tracker <- 'local'
    mapred$mapred.field.separator=" "
    mapred$mapred.textoutputformat.usekey=FALSE
    mapred$mapred.map.tasks=1
    z <- rhmr(map=map, N=N,ofolder=dest,inout=c("lapp","text"),
         mapred=mapred,
         setup=list(map=expression({
             suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(BiocCloud))
             suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(VariantAnnotation))
             suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene))
             suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(snpStats))
         })))
    rhex(z)
    
}

N <- 10
filename <- sprintf("/tmp/%s",paste(sample(letters,6),collapse=""))
makeDataSet(N,filename)
message(sprintf("Input created in %s",filename))

               suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(snpStats))
           })))

So the idea is that the first mapreduce step writes out some input data, and then the second mapreduce step has a mapper that each time it runs, looks at 
a different line of the input data, and writes out a key-value pair where the key is the original line of input data, and the value is some calculation performed
with that input data.

These are the results:

[1] "1 12190 12227 http://s3.amazonaws.com/1000genomes/release/20101123/interim_phase1_release/ALL.chr1.phase1.projectConsensus.genotypes.vcf.gz hg19"

[[1]][[2]]
[1] "28.2006931118756 16.6548562936464 6.55952056101008"

I was hoping there would be 10 results instead of 1 as there were 10 lines of input data. I tried to force the mapper to run more than once by setting mapred.map.tasks but that didn't seem to work.

As I said, I realize this is an awkward way of doing things and I am open to suggestions on how to do it better. But since it "almost" works, I would welcome some advice for getting it to actually work, and would then be  better able to refine the entire process.

Thanks,
Dan

Let me see if I understand correctly.

1) You have a file with N lines in text. 
2) Processing each of the N lines is a lengthy amount of work so you want to it divided into M different chunks so that one mapper isn't working all N lines.  M may be N (the number of lines) or the number of simultaneous mappers you can run or some multiple of the number of mappers you can run.

This job has the characteristic that N is very small, but it implies tons of processing time, so what you can't do is leave the block size of the HDFS determine how the mappers get allocated work.

This is a use case we have thought a fair bit about in the past, but because I haven't been using Rhipe for about 6 months I forget exactly what is most effective. I believe the trick is to do it in the reduce, but that can depend on how your cluster is setup.  

For example,  
Map: each line goes to a key
Reduce: process the line as an input as you were doing before in the map but now in the "reduce$post" part of the reduce expression.


The thing you have to worry about is how the cluster is spreading out the reduce work.  Sometimes hadoop doesn't do what you expect in terms of spreading out very small starting inputs because of "details", and also different clusters have different maximum number of reducers they are configured to use, so this may not be effectively using a cluster set up for many mappers to few reducers.


Good luck,
Jeremiah

I think this is an old question that has been answered.
Use Rhipe_0.73.1 (see code/ directory in Rhipe github)

rhwatch(map, ..., input=rhfmt(type='text', folders="path to input folders", nline=number of lines to process at one time e.g. 10)

if nline = 10, then each mapper will process 10 lines, so if you have 1000 lines and nline==10, then you should have 100 map.tasks.
On Sat, Apr 13, 2013 at 11:54 PM, Jeremiah Rounds <roundsj...@gmail.com> wrote:

Let me see if I understand correctly.

1) You have a file with N lines in text. 
2) Processing each of the N lines is a lengthy amount of work so you want to it divided into M different chunks so that one mapper isn't working all N lines.  M may be N (the number of lines) or the number of simultaneous mappers you can run or some multiple of the number of mappers you can run.

This job has the characteristic that N is very small, but it implies tons of processing time, so what you can't do is leave the block size of the HDFS determine how the mappers get allocated work.

This is a use case we have thought a fair bit about in the past, but because I haven't been using Rhipe for about 6 months I forget exactly what is most effective. I believe the trick is to do it in the reduce, but that can depend on how your cluster is setup.  

For example,  
Map: each line goes to a key
Reduce: process the line as an input as you were doing before in the map but now in the "reduce$post" part of the reduce expression.


The thing you have to worry about is how the cluster is spreading out the reduce work.  Sometimes hadoop doesn't do what you expect in terms of spreading out very small starting inputs because of "details", and also different clusters have different maximum number of reducers they are configured to use, so this may not be effectively using a cluster set up for many mappers to few reducers.


Good luck,
Jeremiah

On Wednesday, June 20, 2012 4:20:04 PM UTC-4, dtenenba wrote:
Hello,
I changed some of the Rhipe examples from the github wiki to do what I want to do, and it works, but it looks like the mapper only runs once, instead of once per piece of input data which is what I would like.
It's also possible that the way I have put my code together is not well thought-out. 

What I did was change the word count generator example to generate some strings of input data to process. 
Then I created another mapreduce job, based on the word count example (with no reduce function, because I don't need one) which takes a piece of that input data and does some processing to it and then writes out some output.
It works but it seems, judging from the output, that the mapper only ran once. 

I realize that maybe I should change this to a single mapreduce job, where the mapper runs just once and creates all the input data, and the reducer processes it. I have tried that and run into problems. So I thought it would be best to post about what actually works and ask how I can get it to work the proper number of times, and then maybe incrementally get to a better way of doing it.

So first, off, some dependencies are required in order to do this, if you want to try it yourself:
You must be running R-2.15.
Do the following:
source("http://bioconductor.org/biocLite.R")
useDevel()
biocLite(c("snpStats", "VariantAnnotation", "TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene"))

Outside of R, do this (because this package is not part of Bioconductor):
svn co --username readonly --password readonly https://hedgehog.fhcrc.org/bioconductor/trunk/madman/Rpacks/BiocCloud/
R CMD INSTALL BiocCloud
(if the above step complains about missing dependencies, install them)

Now, here is what actually works:

Step 1, generate input data:

library(Rhipe)
rhinit()

makeDataSet <- function(N, dest, local=TRUE)
{
    map <- as.expression(bquote({
        N <- .(N)
        urls <- getBucketUrls()
        txdb <- TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene
        cds <- cds(txdb)
        cds <- reduce(keepSeqlevels(cds, paste("chr", 1:22, sep="")))
        values(cds)[["Url"]] <- urls[as.character(seqnames(cds))]
        map <- setNames(sub("chr", "", seqlevels(cds)), seqlevels(cds))
        cds <- renameSeqlevels(cds, map)
        ## Return a regular R list
        tasks <- Map(function(...) list(...), 
            seqnames=as.character(seqnames(cds)), start=start(cds), 
            end=end(cds), url=values(cds)$Url, MoreArgs=list(genome=unique(genome(cds))))

        if (N > length(tasks)) N <- length(tasks)


        for (i in 1:N)
        {
            row = tasks[[i]]
            line <- sprintf("%s %s %s %s %s", row$seqnames, row$start, row$end,
                row$url, row$genome)
            rhcollect(NULL, line)
        }
        
    }, list()))
    mapred <- list()
    if (local) mapred$mapred.job.tracker <- 'local'
    mapred$mapred.field.separator=" "
    mapred$mapred.textoutputformat.usekey=FALSE
    mapred$mapred.map.tasks=1
    z <- rhmr(map=map, N=N,ofolder=dest,inout=c("lapp","text"),
         mapred=mapred,
         setup=list(map=expression({
             suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(BiocCloud))
             suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(VariantAnnotation))
             suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene))
             suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(snpStats))
         })))
    rhex(z)
    
}

N <- 10
filename <- sprintf("/tmp/%s",paste(sample(letters,6),collapse=""))
makeDataSet(N,filename)
message(sprintf("Input created in %s",filename))

## Step 2, process the input data


map <- expression({
    geno <- "GT"
    line <- unlist(strsplit(unlist(map.values)," "))
    seqnames <- line[1]
    start <- as.numeric(line[2])
    end <- as.numeric(line[3])
    url <- line[4]
    genome <- line[5]

    gr <- GRanges(seqnames=seqnames,
        ranges=IRanges(start=start, end=end))
    param <- ScanVcfParam(fixed=c("REF", "ALT"), info=NA, geno=geno,
                          which=gr)

    tab <- open(TabixFile(url))
    on.exit(close(tab))

    vcf <- readVcf(tab, unique(genome), param=param)
    result <- NULL
    if (nrow(vcf)) {
        snpm <- MatrixToSnpMatrix(geno(vcf)[[geno]],
                                  values(fixed(vcf))$REF,
                                  values(fixed(vcf))$ALT)
        result <- col.summary(snpm$genotypes)$z.HWE
    } else result <- numeric()
    keyStr = sprintf("%s %d %d %s %s",
        seqnames, start, end, url, genome)
    valueStr <- character()
    if (length(result)) {
        valueStr <- paste(result, collapse=" ")
    } else {
        valueStr <- "numeric()"
    }
    rhcollect(keyStr, valueStr)
})

outfile <- sprintf("%s-out",filename)


z <- rhmr(map=map, reduce=NA, inout=c("text","sequence")
          ,ifolder=filename
          ,ofolder=outfile,
          mapred=list(mapred.map.tasks=100),
          setup=list(map=expression({
               suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(VariantAnnotation))
               suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(snpStats))
           })))


rhex(z,async=FALSE)

results <- rhread(outfile)

So the idea is that the first mapreduce step writes out some input data, and then the second mapreduce step has a mapper that each time it runs, looks at 
a different line of the input data, and writes out a key-value pair where the key is the original line of input data, and the value is some calculation performed
with that input data.

I was hoping there would be 10 results instead of 1 as there were 10 lines of input data. I tried to force the mapper to run more than once by setting mapred.map.tasks but that didn't seem to work.

As I said, I realize this is an awkward way of doing things and I am open to suggestions on how to do it better. But since it "almost" works, I would welcome some advice for getting it to actually work, and would then be  better able to refine the entire process.

Thanks,
Dan
